conversation.speaker: dialogue
conversation.text:
Police: Part of your statement that day does not match the facts.
Respondent: You’re here again... So you still haven’t found her, right?
Respondent: I’ve also thought carefully about whether any strangers have come here recently... but I really can’t remember.
Respondent: You’re right... In fact, Minghao did come here that day.
Respondent: I’m sorry, I lied. I didn’t think it was particularly important information.
Respondent: Minghao is a good child... I was worried that if I told you, you might form a bad impression of him.
Respondent: I shouldn’t have meddled and caused you trouble. I’m truly sorry.
Respondent: Minghao came over at around 3:30.
Respondent: When he came in, he seemed the same as usual, just a bit anxious. I asked him about it, and he said he had to go back right away and didn’t say anything more.
Respondent: As usual, he picked a bag of candy. I thought to myself: it seems he came to buy candy for his younger sister again today.
Respondent: Xiyuan especially likes that kind of candy—the pink kind that makes your cheeks puff up like a hamster after you put it in your mouth.
Respondent: I’ve told you before that Minghao is a very steady child.
Respondent: But he was very strange that day. He held the candy and squatted in front of the card display counter, lingering there for a long time.
Respondent: Then he came to the cashier and paid for the candy.
Respondent: But he kept his head down and didn’t dare to look at me.
Respondent: I felt something was odd, so after he left, I went to check the counter.
Respondent: ...And then I discovered.
Respondent: One card was missing from the counter.
Respondent: That kid—I thought to myself that next time I saw him, I would definitely teach him a good lesson.
Respondent: But when I thought about how long he had hesitated there...
Respondent: I just felt really uncomfortable inside.
